# <span id="aanchor257"></span> System Configuration

[&lt;&lt; Back](System%20Configuration.md) \| [General](System%20Configuration.md) \| [Approvals](System%20Configuration%20-%20Approvals%20Tab.md) \| [Thresholds](System%20Configuration%20-%20Thresholds%20Tab.md)

## General Tab



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 610;height: 520;" />

The General tab contains the following options:

- **Allow free-form Edit Reason Entry** - When enabled, you can enter custom edit reasons when editing data; otherwise, you must select from pre-defined edit reasons. (See: [Edit Reason Editor](../../Application/Edit%20Reason%20Editor.md))

- **Require Edit Reason for Exceptions** - When enabled, you must select an edit reason when updating the status of an exception from the [Exception Resolver](../../../Exceptions/Exception%20Resolver/Exception%20Resolver.md).

  Updating an exception’s status from any screen other than the Exception Resolver will not prompt for an edit reason; however, a default edit reason is generated automatically.

- **Validate When Exception(s) Acknowledged** - When enabled, validations are run if an exception status is changed to or from "Acknowledged", "Pending", or "Unresolved" in the Exception Resolver. This enables the application to maintain an accurate count of exceptions for each meter periodic in the final form tables.

  This requires additional processing time, so if this count is not needed, do not enable this option.

- **Do Not Close if Missing Data** - When enabled, meters that have missing data cannot be closed when the meter is in an active state. A meter is considered to be missing data if the completion status on the meter’s final form monthly record is “Incomplete”, or if there is no final form monthly record rolled up.

- **Do Not Close if Pending Exceptions** - When enabled, meters and tickets with unresolved or pending exceptions cannot be closed.

- **Update GMS Date on Close** - When enabled, the close process updates the <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCTextPopup MCTextPopupHotSpot MCTextPopup_Open glossaryTerm MCTextPopupHotSpot_" alt="Closed" data-mc-alt2="Open">GMS Date<span class="MCTextPopupBody popupBody"><span class="MCTextPopupArrow"></span>The gas measurement system day on which a database record was created or last modified</span></a> in the final form tables when data is closed. This option may not always be desirable since the data (volume, energy, etc.) did not actually change.

<!-- -->

- **Allow Closed Meters to be Reopened** - When enabled, meters that have been closed can be re-opened if no prior period adjustments (PPAs) have been applied. If you want to require a PPA rather than allow meters to be re-opened, do not enable this option.

- **Allow Import Against Inactive Meters** - When enabled, you can import data for an inactive meter. FLOWCAL will generate [Exception 17003](../../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/17000/17000-17999.md), and the data will not be rolled up. You must then determine if the data is valid and decide whether to set the status to Active for the associated time frame.

- **Allow Import Against Disconnected Meters** - When enabled, you can import data for a disconnected meter. FLOWCAL will generate [Exception 17004](../../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/17000/17000-17999.md), and the data will not be rolled up. You must then determine if the data is valid and decide whether to set the status to Active for the associated time frame.

- **Inhibit Source Analysis with Exceptions** - When enabled, analysis records with exceptions will be inhibited and not used for source apply operations. These exceptions are triggered on records that fall outside of the validation set points specified in the Quality Source Editors.

- **Do Not Extend Source Analysis on Import** - When enabled, if a source analysis record does not contain an end date on import, the end date will end at the start of the next source analysis record. If disabled(default), the end date will extend to the end of time, overwriting existing records.

- **Source Assignments Required** - When enabled, [exception 55](../../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/0-999/0-99.md) will be generated for any meter that does not include a source assignment for dates after the first flow date (as provided on the [Misc. tab](../../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Misc%20Tab.md) of the Meter Editor). When an assignment is created, the exception is automatically resolved.

  The meter must have an assignment for all of time, so the first assignment will cover all of time, regardless of what is selected for the duration. You can then split the assignment as long as there is an assignment that covers all of time.

  Time periods during which the meter status is non-existent do not require a source assignment.

- **Skip Assign for Ext Vol Meters** - When enabled, source assignments are not required for meters designated as External Volume in the Meter Editor. (This option is used in conjunction with the Source Assignments Required option.)

- **Use Calculated Results for Samples** - When enabled, imported values for standalone sample mix properties (e.g., relative density, molar mass) will be discarded and replaced with calculated values.

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Rail Car Level">Default Rail Car Level

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Rail Car Level">

  This feature requires the **Liquids** add-on.

  When entering a rail car ticket in the Ticket Editor, there is a field for the level on the car that the loaders are trying to hit. Use these fields to specify a default level and associated units, rather than manually entering this value each time. (Applicable to rail car tickets only.)

  </div>

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="TESTit Integrated">TESTit Integration

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="TESTit Integrated">

  This feature requires TESTit 2 Integrated.

  - **Allow Reschedule of Analysis Samples** - When enabled, a TESTit sample test is scheduled or rescheduled when source analysis records are inhibited due to exceptions generated when data falls outside of the validation boundaries.
  - **TESTit Analysis Sample Task** - Specify the task type to schedule (used in conjunction with the Allow Reschedule of Analysis Samples option).

  </div>

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Flow Time Edits">Flow Time Edits

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Flow Time Edits">

  Specify whether the Volume Editor will display meter flow time as a percentage or as a clock time.

  For percentage of flow, the amount of time represented by a percentage is dependent on the data resolution set in the meter's characteristics. For example: If the data resolution is hourly, 100% corresponds to one hour. If the data resolution is daily, 100% corresponds to one day.

  </div>

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Flow Time Calc">Flow Time Calculation Method

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Flow Time Calc">

  - **Simple (0 or 100%)** - If the differential pressure is greater than 0 or volume is greater than 0, flow time is assumed to be the full duration of the record; otherwise, flow time is assumed to be 0.
  - **Extension/Sqrt(DP\*SP)** - Static pressure is in psia; differential pressure is pressure in inches of water.
  - **Extention/Sqrt(DP\*SP\*1/T)** - Static pressure is in psia; differential pressure is pressure in inches of water; temperature is in Rankine.

  </div>

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Mol%">Mol % Normalization

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Mol%">

  Source analyses can be enabled to normalize imported samples if the total mole percent is not 100% but is within a minimum and maximum value. The Mol % Normalization option is enabled within Validations in Quality Source Editor, by choosing to use System or Source Quality limits. If System or Source Quality is selected, but min/max limits are not specified, these system-level limits will be used.

  </div>

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Pulses Display">Pulses Display

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Pulses Display">

  - **Pulses Display/(Decimals)** - The number of decimal places to display for pulses (up to four decimals).
  - **Days Past End Date (Days)** - The number of days into the future (past the current date) that positive displacement data can be manually entered on the Positive Displacement Entry screens.

  </div>

- <span id="ExceptionValues"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Exception Values">Exception Values

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Exception Values">

  - **Pct. Flow in 1 Hour (%)** - For orifice and cone meters, if the flow time (as a percentage of an hour) is greater than this value, an exception is generated (default value is 100.09%).
  - **Pct. Flow in 1 Day (%)** - For orifice and cone meters, if the total flow time in the day (as a percentage of an hour) is greater than this value, an exception is generated. For a full day of flow, 2400 would be the expected value (default value is 2400.20%).
  - **Low Flow Cut-Off** - If an orifice or cone meter does not have a low flow cutoff at the meter level, this value is used (default value is 0.00).
  - **Beta Ratio MIN** - If the beta ratio (orifice or cone diameter/tube diameter) is less than this value, an exception is generated (default value is 0.10).
  - **Beta Ration MAX** - If the beta ratio (orifice or cone diameter/tube diameter) is greater than this value, an exception is generated (default value is 0.75).
  - **MIN Pressure** - If the static pressure in psia or kPa is below this value, an exception is generated (default value is 1.00).
  - **Weekly Resolution (Days)** - Used for orifice chart meters as the maximum length of a record for meters with weekly resolution specified in meter characteristics.
  - **Monthly Resolution (Days)** - Used for orifice chart meters as the maximum length of a record for meters with monthly resolution specified in meter characteristics.

  </div>

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon" data-mc-targets="External Volume Import"></a><span id="ExternalVolume"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="External Volume Import">External Volume Import

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="External Volume Import">

  - **Input conditions must match database** - When enabled, you must enter the pressure base, heating value condition, data span, and data resolution on the initial selection window when navigating to Manual Entry \> Meter Input. If these values do not match what is in the database, you will not be allowed to continue.

  - **Can enter data for any meter** - When enabled, you can enter external volume data for any meter, regardless of whether the meter is identified as external volume in the Meter Editor. When this option is disabled, you can only enter data for meters that are flagged as external volume.

  - **Allow overwrite of existing data** - When enabled, existing data will be overwritten with new data. The new data will go in as original data (revision 0) and the previously imported data will be removed.

    This is for meters that:

    - Are marked as "External Volume" in the Meter Editor.

    - Contain data that was previously imported and has no edits (including source apply and auto edits).

      This option is intended for third-party measurement where the third party providing the data makes edits to the data, an audit trail is not required, and only the final answer reported by the third party is needed.

    When this option is enabled and Create Revisions set to "No", overwriting data will become revision 0. If Creation Revisions set to "Yes<span style="color: #5d5d5d;">",</span> overwriting data will increment the revision number.

    When this option is not enabled, you will not be able to import into a month that already has data. The import process window will display “No new history found”.

    For non-external volume meters, once data is imported, FLOWCAL does not overwrite the data on import.

  - **Season starts on** - External volume meters can have default temperature values set up for the different seasons when data is entered manually, as well as year-round defaults for static pressure and heating value. The start of each season must be defined so the appropriate values are applied when editing the data.

    The start of the season is set from the [External Volume Default Values Editor](../../../Imports/Manual%20Entry/External%20Volume%20Default%20Values%20Editor.md).

    See also: [Manual Meter Input](../../../Imports/Manual%20Entry/Manual%20Meter%20Input.md)

  </div>

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="GPS Ranges">GPS Ranges

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="GPS Ranges">

  Use these options to define limits to represent geographic boundaries. If latitude and longitude values that are outside of these system limits are entered in the Meter Editor, a message will display.

  </div>

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Location Rollups">Location Rollups

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Location Rollups">

  These options can increase the size of your database.

  - **Calculate Weekly Totals** - When enabled, if a weekly schedule is assigned to a location in the Location Editor, Location Rollups will total values based on the weekly schedule, as well as calculating hourly, daily, and monthly totals. Location Rollups do not calculate weekly totals by default.

    A weekly schedule can be assigned to a location, tank, inventory, liquid cavern or comparison. These options allow for Location Rollups to calculate values that span multiple days, but less than a month per the defined schedule.

    Although referred to as Weekly Totals, the span does not have to be for a week. The customized time span can be defined in the Annual Schedule Editor.

  </div>

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Location Comments">Location Comments

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Location Comments">

  Location comments are also known as location edit reasons. When a given location type (i.e. Balance, Inventory, Segment, or Station) is checked, you will be prompted for an edit reason when modifying the respective location type in the Location Editor.

  </div>

- <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerRightIcon MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_RightIcon MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Additional Saturation Values">Additional Saturation Values

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /></a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Additional Saturation Values">

  Contact <a href="mailto:flowcal.support@quorumsoftware.com" class="notelink">Support</a> before enabling this option. Turning on this functionality will greatly increase the size of your database.

  Saturation conditions are the amount of water vapor in the gas at various conditions, ranging from dry to saturated. Volume and energy at additional saturation conditions can be calculated and stored in the final form tables.

  When enabled, volume and energy is calculated at the respective saturation condition(s).

  - Dry Condition
  - Saturated @ Flowing
  - Saturated @ Base
  - Partially Saturated

  This information only exists in the database and does not get reported.

  </div>
